messages:
sarah: Quick question — my sister had an unexpected early delivery and I need to start leave next week to help with the newborn and her 3yo. Can I take intermittent parental leave for sibling caregiving? What paperwork/payroll cutoffs should I watch for? 🙏

devon: Hey Sarah — sorry to hear, hope everyone’s ok. Short answer: we don’t have a separate ‘sibling parental leave’ bucket, but you may be eligible for caregiving under FMLA (if you meet eligibility) or our short-term caregiving policy. Either way we can set up intermittent leave.

michelle: Also FYI we have backup-care stipend and flexible partial-pay top-up options for caregiving situations. If you’ll be doing days on/off, intermittent is usually the right route.

sarah: I’m eligible for FMLA (been here > 12 months) but not sure how to document placement/medical need since it’s a newborn and not adoption. What exactly do you need?

devon: For FMLA caregiving for a family member, we typically need a healthcare provider certification listing need for care and approximate dates. For newborn support, a brief note from the parent (your sister) explaining expected involvement and dates is fine in addition to the HCP form. Please send both to leave-requests@redwood.com.

michelle: Payroll/benefits timing: to have the leave start reflected on the next pay run we need the completed leave request + HCP uploaded by Wednesday 11:59pm PT (that’s the payroll cutoff). If you miss that you can still start leave but payroll/top-up might apply on the following cycle. Also ping me if you want the benefit premiums to be continued by the company while you’re on unpaid leave — that’s a one-time request we can submit.

sarah: Awesome — thanks. If I go intermittent (2–3 full days/week) does my manager need to approve FTE/coverage and backfill?

jason: I’m her manager — I can cover product demos and reassign on-call for that period. If we need >2 weeks full-time coverage we’d ask for a temporary contractor budget; happy to approve within my team.

devon: Manager approval is required for scheduling and backfill spend. For short intermittent patterns we usually avoid hiring and shuffle priorities. If you anticipate > 30 cumulative days in a quarter, we’ll fast-track a backfill conversation.

michelle: Practical next steps: 1) Sarah upload HCP + sister note to Workday (or email leave-requests@redwood.com) 2) confirm exact dates with Jason 3) People Ops will create the leave entry and flag payroll before Wed cutoff.

# snippet for email (paste):
```
To: leave-requests@redwood.com
Subject: Leave request — Sarah (Intermittent caregiving)
Body: Attached HCP form + family statement. Desired start date: 2026-04-06. Intermittent pattern: Mon/Tue every week for ~6 weeks. Please confirm.
```

peopleops-bot: Ticket created: LEAVE-3245 — status: awaiting-docs (assigned to devon).

sarah: Sending docs now, thanks everyone. One last Q — does the backup-care stipend cover nighttime nanny for the first two weeks?

michelle: Backup-care stipend can be used for short-term nanny or in-home care depending on vendor coverage. We’ll need receipts to reimburse. I can DM you the vendor list and exception process if needed.

devon: Got the email and HCP — we’ll confirm with payroll once processed. Jason — if you could mark the team calendar and let UX know about demo swaps that’d help.

jason: Done — marked calendar and asked UX to hold off on new feature demos that week. Good luck Sarah, text if you need anything. :heart:
